Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — great context on the ledger reconciliation workflows and where you want automation to surface in the UI. Below is a concise recap + recommended next steps so we can get a tech deep-dive scheduled: 

Recap (short):
- Goal: Replace manual reconciliation emails with an automated assistant that can call internal tools (transaction lookup, exception ticketing) and surface structured results to your ops UI.
- Key constraints: PCI-scope data, 99th %ile latency target ~400ms for user-facing flows, need deterministic auth routing (prod vs sandbox).

Integration topics we discussed (actionable items):
1) SDK & auth: We support our SDK (JS/Go/Python) and recommend using service-account-based keys for server-side tool calls. For browser flows we suggest a short-lived token exchange (AuthN via your IdP -> Redwood token). See attachment for diagram.
2) Routing & model variants: Use policy-based routing to send sensitive workloads to your Private deployment (or Dedicated pool) and fall back to hosted when allowed. We can preset routing rules by route name / tag.
3) Tool/function calling patterns:
   - Tool definitions: describe inputs/outputs (JSON schema) up front — Redwood will validate and return structured results for deterministic parsing.
   - Tool choice & parallelism: for lookups we recommend fan-out to parallel read-only tools (transaction lookup + enrichment service) and then an aggregation step that merges results.
   - Error handling: return structured error codes from tools; use retries with idempotency keys for transient failures and a safe fallback prompt when downstream tools are unavailable.
4) Embeddings & rerankers: We recommend a small, dense embedding index (512-d) for fast semantic retrieval, with a lightweight reranker model if you need strong precision on top-k.

Immediate next steps:
- Please confirm whether we should prepare a short SDK sample for server-side auth (JS or Python).
- If procurement is required, Vivek can share our mutual action plan template and standard SOW language.
- Proposed: 60-min technical deep-dive next week (we can demo code + run a sample tool call).

Attaching: redwood-integration-overview.pdf (architecture diagram)

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your timeline.

—

Sam —

Great questions — answers & a short snippet below. I attached a 1-page pre-read to the Drive link in the thread.

1) SDK snippet (Python, server-side) — defining a tool and calling it (simplified):

```python
# pseudo-code, simplified for clarity
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<SERVICE_KEY>")

# Tool definition (registered in your workspace)
transaction_lookup_tool = {
  "name": "transaction_lookup",
  "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"tx_id": {"type": "string"}}},
  "output_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"status": {"type": "string"}, "amount": {"type": "number"}}}
}

# Call the tool as part of a function calling workflow
response = client.call_tool("transaction_lookup", {"tx_id": "abc-123"}, idempotency_key="tx-abc-123")
if response.code == 200:
  data = response.json()
else:
  # structured error handling
  if response.code in [502, 503]:
    # transient -> retry with backoff (idempotency ensures safe retry)
    ...
  else:
    # permanent -> return user-safe fallback
    ...
```

2) Parallel tools & ordering:
- Pattern: fan-out read-only calls in parallel (no side-effects) to enrichment services. Use an aggregation step that merges by key (tx_id) and timestamps. For side-effecting calls (e.g., create-ticket) do a single canonical writer to avoid duplicates; use idempotency keys and a write-queue if ordering matters.
- If your enrichment services return out-of-order, include a sequence/timestamp field in the tool outputs and reconcile in the aggregator.

3) Embedding hosting tradeoffs:
- Managed Redwood vector store: simplest, lower ops, fast network latency to hosted model; we provide eviction/refresh helpers.
- Self-hosted in VPC: lowest network exposure, can be colocated with your DB for microsecond-range lookups, but you’ll manage scaling / replication. If your latency SLO is tight (400ms end-to-end), colocating the index in your VPC + using our private routing is a solid option.

I can put together a short tech deck showing these patterns and a sample repo. Want JS + Python samples?

—
Marissa
